item.title: @AnthropicAI：Anthropic公布可解释性研究新进展探讨开源模型中的神经元基础
item.description:
New Anthropic Fellows research: Returning to the neuron basis for interpretability

Understanding what’s happening inside an AI model helps to make it safer. One obvious place to look is its neurons, or the simple units it’s built from. Early interpretability work did just that, but over the past couple years, researchers largely moved on from that idea, for three reasons: a single neuron often fires on several unrelated inputs, the way a concept is represented can change between two layers of neurons within a single model, and facts seem to be spread across many neurons.

We re-examined these problems by looking at what each neuron contributed to the model’s outputs, not just what caused that neuron to fire. All three problems turned out to be smaller than assumed. Neurons rarely add two unrelated concepts at once, their outputs mean roughly the same thing across most layers, and facts, though widely distributed across neurons, are still readable.

In a second post, we put these findings to use. With no extra training, neurons in open-weight models helped us to detect harmful text, steer behavior, and find hidden behaviors in finetuned models.

Part 1: https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/neuron-basis-theory/
Part 2: https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/neuron-basis-applications/

item.title: @AnthropicAI：Anthropic发布AI智能体沙箱逃逸研究评估模型Siren及相关数据
item.description:
New Anthropic research: When an AI agent can escape its sandbox, will it choose to?

Our new evaluation, Siren, gives Claude routine tasks in intentionally weakened sandboxes, with something useful to the task left outside of the sandbox. Across 1,700+ scenarios built to tempt them, recent Claude models accessed, tried to access, or looked outside the sandbox 21-32% of the time, but they rarely misused what they found. However, when the system prompt described both the sandbox and its rules, that rate dropped to about 2% or less.

We also used Siren to calibrate Claude Code’s auto mode, which checks commands before they run, so Claude can work without asking permission at every step.

Read our blog for more detail: https://safeguards.anthropic.com/2026/siren/

item.title: 【回复】@OpenAI：OpenAI公布GPT-6.2湿实验室验证数据：多款设计蛋白质与抗体显示结合活性
item.description:
回复 @OpenAI
Performance improved across model generations.

In computer tests, an internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein tasks, including designing shapes and predicting how molecules fit together.

The models’ written reasoning and code suggest they draw on math, physics, chemistry and biological knowledge to work through these problems.
原帖

回复 @OpenAI
Scientists design proteins to develop new biotechnologies and potential medicines. The challenge is turning a goal, such as blocking a signal involved in disease, into a protein with the shape and sequence needed to do that job.

This often takes many specialized models, each with limits on the instructions it can accept. A general-purpose model could let researchers guide this work in ordinary language and introduce new requirements simply by changing the prompt.
原帖

回复 @OpenAI
We tested that control at scales ranging from a single bond between two atoms to a protein’s overall shape.

For GPT-6.2, a prompt could identify which two atoms formed a bond between a small molecule and a protein, then ask how the rest of the molecule fit. Other prompts specified where a new protein should attach and how many coils or strands to include.
原帖

回复 @OpenAI
With our research partner Onava, we also tested two parts of protein design in the lab.

GPT-6.2 designed the protein shapes. Specialized models filled in the rest of the workflow. Of 322 proteins tested, 35 showed evidence of binding, or attachment, with binders for all five targets.
原帖

回复 @OpenAI
In a separate experiment, GPT-6.2 designed new sequences for three shapes it had previously designed. 14 of 107 proteins made with the new sequences showed binding in the wet lab.

GPT-6.2 also redesigned the parts of antibodies that grip a target. In two further laboratory experiments, 128 of 182 redesigned small antibodies and 179 of 272 redesigned antibody fragments retained binding.
原帖

回复 @OpenAI
This is a proof of concept. Next, we want to test whether these proteins do something useful after attaching, tackle harder targets, and extend the work to other types of molecules.

Our goal is for scientists to one day design working medicines simply by prompting. We want to accelerate both the protein design cycle and reduce the number of experiments needed to find a functional protein.

item.title: 【回复】@arena：研究显示AI智能体常在决策时询问用户并探讨其背后的行为原因
item.description:
回复 @arena
Do you ever wish your agent would just get on with work instead of asking questions?

We call this behavior “decision-dodging”: handing a decision back to you when the agent should have just acted on your behalf and wrapped up the task.

To understand how often it happens in practice, we selected 20 Agent Arena models across major labs.

We then counted a decision as obvious when the agent asked about something it could have decided itself, and the user simply told it to go ahead. We found that:

- Kimi K3.1 Pro by @Kimi_Moonshot and three of @OpenAI’s models (GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra) dodge the least. They handed back an obvious decision in just 2% of sessions.

- @OpenAI’s models as a group dodge about half as often as those from @GoogleDeepMind, @AIatMeta or @AnthropicAI. They do so in around 3% of sessions, against around 5%.

- Claude Fable 5.1 is the worst offender. It handed back an obvious decision in 7.5% of sessions, the most of any model. It asked users to decide in 20% of sessions, and 40% of those questions were obvious.

To find out more, and see how Fable 5.2 compares to 5.1, see the video below.
原帖

回复 @arena
In addition to comparing models on decision-dodging, we also wanted to investigate why this happens.

Of sessions with an obvious decision:

- 53% had the agent asking if it should keep going
- 37% had it offering extra work that users simply accepted
- 21% had it asking which way to go, on calls it could have made itself

Where does this come from?

Today’s agents are tuned to check in with people, offer ideas and respect their preferences. But they’re also meant to finish the job without hand-holding. The two pull in opposite directions, and agents can land on the wrong side of that line.

And if it happens too often, remember there are other agents that may work better for you.
原帖

This isn’t good for the ecosystem! It leaves us susceptible to failure modes that are hard to anticipate, and narrows our collective imagination of what AI assistants could be like. item.title: 【回复】@OpenAI：天文学家通过Codex程序在开普勒望远镜数据中发现疑似系外行星信号
item.description:
回复 @OpenAI
Two amateur astronomers, Kevin Bond (@canvrno) and Ethan Byrd (@itsjustemail), independently found signals that could point to planets around distant stars. They knew you didn't need your own telescope for this kind of hunt.

Kevin used Codex and Ethan used Astra to search public telescope data for tiny, recurring dips in starlight that an orbiting planet can cause. Both found signals worth a second look.
原帖

回复 @OpenAI
Kevin used Codex to build a program that searched for observations of about 100,000 stars from NASA’s Kepler telescope. One star in the constellation Lyra dimmed every 13.8 days. If a planet is causing that dip, the amount of light it blocks suggests it could be about 2.4 times as wide as Earth.

An astronomer at the SETI Institute independently found the same signal and one other that Kevin had flagged. For the star in Lyra, astronomers now know when to watch for the next dip.
原帖

回复 @OpenAI
Ethan asked Astra to review published methods and write software to search observations of about 19 million stars from NASA’s TESS mission. The search included regions around a star where a planet with the right atmosphere could have liquid water on its surface.

His first pass turned up 49 candidates. He sent one of the most promising to researchers on NASA’s TESS mission, where it’s awaiting a closer look.

Explore Kevin and Ethan’s findings and learn how to get started: http://openai.com/index/searching-for-distant-planets-with-astra/

item.description:
GPT-6.2 Astra for solving a significant historical mystery:

@HistoryGPT：In testing GPT-6.2, I used it to make a significant historical discovery which I detail in the post below. This suggests that the process of research and discovery we’re already seeing in verifiable domains like math is starting to generalize to non-deterministic fields like history.

You can read the full post here:

https://generativehistory.substack.com/p/gpt-62-astra-solves-a-historical

In a nutshell, Yale’s Beinecke Library holds an anonymous sketchbook of an 1808 journey from Montreal to Lake Superior and back. I’ve spent many hours over the years trying to figure out who made the sketches with no luck. The artist could literally be any one of several thousand people. There are few clues: only four dated and labelled images.

With minimal prompting, in just 22 minutes, Astra used publicly available sources to identify a minor French aristocrat, the vicomte de Chabot, as the artist and suggested that we test the hypothesis by ordering copies of a little known microfilmed diary of Chabot’s trip it also found.

I was truly stunned. I’d never heard of Chabot or this diary! New document finds are also exceedingly rare in a well worn field like fur trade history.

I ordered scans of the journal from microfilm and when they arrived the handwriting matched the captions in the sketchbook. item.title: @ArtificialAnlys：Artificial Analysis发布编码智能体基准测试：评估不同运行框架对模型成本与性能的影响
item.description:
Launching Harness Comparisons on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index: the best harness varies between models, and harness choice has a greater impact on cost than score

Harness Comparisons hold the model fixed and change only the harness, to show how the harness affects a model's performance. We ran @OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna and @Zai_org's GLM-5.3-Flash at max reasoning effort in 13 harnesses each, across v2.1 of the Coding Agent Index.

Key takeaways:

➤ No single harness is best across models: performance depends on the harness and model as a pair. GPT-6 Luna scores highest in Codex (26), OpenAI's own harness, which ranks last with GLM-5.3-Flash. GLM-5.3-Flash scores highest in Claude Code (39), which ranks 6th with GPT-6 Luna

➤ The harnesses that offer the best performance per dollar differ by model: with GPT-6 Luna they are Pi (21 at $0.11 per task), mini-swe-agent (25 at $0.16) and Codex (26 at $0.19). With GLM-5.3-Flash they are Mistral Vibe (37 at $0.38), Kimi Code CLI (37 at $0.56) and Claude Code (39 at $0.58). No harness is on the Pareto frontier for both models

➤ The harness has a greater impact on cost than score: 11 of 13 harnesses score 20 to 26 with GPT-6 Luna and 10 of 13 score 35 to 39 with GLM-5.3-Flash. Cost per task ranges from $0.11 in Pi to $0.62 in Muse Code with GPT-6 Luna, and from $0.38 in Mistral Vibe to $0.91 in Devin CLI with GLM-5.3-Flash

➤ GLM-5.3-Flash reasons differently inside Codex: it reasons in terse fragments in Codex and in full prose in the other 12 harnesses, and produces 52k output tokens per task in Codex, compared with 97k to 202k elsewhere. We believe this contributes to its lowest performance occurring in the Codex harness

item.title: @mingchikuo：Analysis of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and remaining market uncertainties
item.description:
Analysis of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO:

1. Uncertainty removed:
Mainly company strategy, product roadmap, tech development, and supply chain management. This overhang weighed on tech stocks over the past 1–2 weeks, so shares surged as soon as it was removed. But whether they return to prior highs depends not only on each company's position in the AI supply chain and Nvidia's ecosystem, but also on the two points below.

2. Uncertainties that remain:
(1) Sales: The impact on Nvidia's shipments and revenue after tighter US controls on AI GPU exports and overseas compute leasing.
(2) Circular financing: The impact of higher compliance costs and stricter reviews on ongoing and future deals.
(3) Investigations, lawsuits, and stricter oversight: Jensen and Nvidia are still under investigation. Future public comments, internal decisions, and external interactions will all become part of the investigation and new evidence for questioning. This also adds to the sales and circular financing uncertainty above.

3. Real-world bottlenecks that can't be changed:
(1) Data center buildout challenges (power, labor, etc.) and stricter related regulations ahead.
(2) CSP capex peaking one by one in 2027–2028.
(3) Manufacturing tech limits (e.g., next-gen advanced packaging yields).

item.title: 【回复】@EpochAIResearch：Epoch AI因模拟漏洞和奖励造假将Vending-Bench 2评为有缺陷
item.description:
回复 @EpochAIResearch
We are publishing 4 new benchmark reviews: 1 benchmark is Verified, 3 are Flawed. Another 4 benchmarks lacked sufficient information to assign a verdict.

🟩 Verified: the benchmark can broadly be interpreted as described by the developer, and any errors don’t substantially affect results. We publish a full review, including weaknesses and limitations.

🟥 Flawed: the benchmark has one or more substantive flaws users need to know about to interpret results, most often >20% of tasks with accuracy-impacting errors. We publish a limited write-up of the flaws.

⬛ Not Enough Info: we couldn’t access enough to assign a verdict. Developers get a week to respond before we apply this label.

Details from Verified and Flawed reviews are below, along with a link to our full rubric.
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
MazeBench v1.1 is a benchmark that measures spatial and long-horizon reasoning in a 3D maze environment. The benchmark is well designed, with many strengths and only minor weaknesses. We designate it as Verified.

Read our full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/mazebench/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
ARC-AGI-3 is an interactive reasoning benchmark designed to measure AI agents’ ability to explore new environments and adapt their strategy across increasingly difficult levels of multiple games. It is scored via action efficiency relative to a variable human baseline, but models are never told to be action efficient.

This means it measures a mixture of capability and propensity towards efficiency. Overall, it failed our criteria for scoring, benchmark consistency, model elicitation (in the official ‘Standard’ harness), and bias in evaluation setup and earned a Flawed designation.

Full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/arc-agi-3/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 is a benchmark designed to measure agents’ ability to perform long-horizon, economically valuable tasks with verifiable outcomes. Unfortunately, at least 44% of the tasks we sampled had severe errors. We designate the benchmark as Flawed.

Full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/agents-last-exam/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
Vending-Bench 2 is a benchmark designed to test agents’ ability to run a simulated vending machine over a year. We designated the benchmark as Flawed due to issues with the simulation, vulnerability to reward-hacking, and uneven evaluation setups.

Full review: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/vending-bench-2/review
原帖

回复 @EpochAIResearch
Benchmarks assess AI capabilities, but their quality varies substantially. We hope to be a consistent source of information on benchmark quality.

See all of our reviews: https://epoch.ai/data/benchmark-reviews-documentation/included-benchmarks

Full rubric: https://epoch.ai/data/benchmark-reviews-documentation/methodology
